name: Castello Banfi Wine Resort
positioning: A hotel in the restored medieval castle of Poggio alle Mura on the Banfi wine estate, between Siena and the Maremma, with winery tours and tastings
best_for: Wine lovers who want winery tours and tastings on the estate
Travelers drawn to medieval history and architecture
Guests with a car who want to explore Val d'Orcia villages

facts.text: The castle of Poggio alle Mura has a strategic location between Siena and the Maremma.
The castle complex developed mostly between the 9th and 13th centuries, though its origin is earlier.
The Counts Placidi, a family of Sienese nobles, ruled the castle from 1529 until 1959.
In 1983 the castle became part of the Banfi vineyard estate, and the Mariani family, owners of the winery, restored it after the acquisition.
The fortress has a compact square plan with two inner courtyards and a crenellated watchtower on the northern flank.
A marble slab on the entrance portal bears notations about work done to the courtyard in 1654.
Castello Banfi brings together the hotel, two restaurants, the Enoteca, the Balsameria and the Glass Museum.
Public winery tours last about an hour and are followed by a wine pairing lunch at La Taverna or a wine tasting at L'Enoteca.
Wines that can be tasted include Brunello di Montalcino, Bolgheri, Chianti, Chianti Classico, SuperTuscans and whites, as well as wines from Piedmont.
Val d'Orcia, around the resort, offers trekking, cycling and horseback riding.
The wine bar inside the Enoteca pairs Banfi wines with Tuscan fare such as platters of local cured meats and cheeses.

highlights.text: The fifteenth-century courtyard has low arches on octagonal pillars, and outside stands a rare and ancient ice-house with a characteristic mound shape.
Dungeons dug into the tufa are still visible, and finds from the last restoration suggest a settlement already in Etruscan times.
The private Discovering Excellence Tour covers vineyards, the wine cellar and an exclusive tasting.
Pienza, the Abbey of Sant'Antimo, Sant'Angelo in Colle, Camigliano, Sasso d'Ombrone and Castiglione d'Orcia are villages to visit while staying at the resort.

considerations.text: The winery is 4 km from the castle, and guests on the public tour need their own car to follow the guide there.
Advance reservation is mandatory for the public winery tours.
WhataHotel notes the remote location requires a car for exploring nearby towns.
